abstract: Roots play a central role in soil organic matter (SOM) formation, stabilization and decomposition, yet how roots and soil properties modulate these dynamics is poorly understood. We used ingrowth cores to investigate how roots influence particulate organic matter (POM) and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM) in forest plots dominated by arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (EcM) trees in Indiana (IN) and New York (NY), USA. Additionally, we amended a subset of cores with nutrients or water (controls) to examine how nutrient availability affects root-induced changes in POM and MAOM at a moderately N-limited site (IN) and a strongly N-limited site (NY). We tested three hypotheses: H1) root-induced changes in SOM fractions differ between tree-mycorrhizal types, with EcM roots promoting POM losses and AM roots enhancing MAOM gains, H2) increases in nutrient availability reduce POM loss and enhance MAOM formation, with the greatest changes occurring at the most N-limiting environments (NY), and H3) root-induced changes in POM and MAOM fluctuate over time, as initial gains in SOM are offset by SOM losses. We found partial support for H1 and H2 and modest support for H3. For H1, POM-C losses outpaced MAOM gains in EcM-dominated plots (as hypothesized) but both SOM fractions were mostly unchanged in AM-dominated plots. For H2, nitrogen addition did not increase POM-C (as hypothesized), but it did increase MAOM-C modestly in AM plots and EcM plots at the more N-limited (NY). In support of H3, MAOM gains observed after 24 months had generally diminished by 35 months. This was especially true for MAOM-N at the NY site which declined by 13.4%. Together, our results show that roots can simultaneously accelerate losses from POM and promote MAOM accumulation, and that tree-mycorrhizal type, environmental context and time modulate these effects. Additionally, our study suggests that short-term studies of root-SOM interactions may provide an incomplete view of soil C persistence drivers in forests, which can change dynamically over time.

metadata.title: Tree roots drive POM losses and transient MAOM gains across AM and ECM stands

summary: Ingrowth-core experiments in AM and EcM forests in Indiana and New York show roots drive POM loss and transient MAOM gains, modulated by nitrogen and time.
title: Tree roots drive POM losses and transient MAOM gains across AM and ECM stands
